q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of terracotta planters and pottery?
title: Terracotta planter footprint per piece
short: Record the kiln fuel per firing, such as wood, coal or gas, and divide by good pieces fired. Add clay digging and transport diesel, wheel or press electricity, and packing. Firing is usually most of the figure; wood CO2 is reported separately as biogenic.

ul: Clay, dug or bought, and the diesel to bring it.
Kiln fuel: wood, sawdust, coal or LPG.
Pug mill, potter's wheels or jigger machines.
Drying, then firing in an updraft, downdraft or gas kiln.
Breakage, which raises the fuel per good piece.

p: Report per piece by size, and say how firing fuel was shared between sizes in the same load, such as by weight.

example.title: Worked example: pottery unit per piece (one month)
lines: Kiln coal: 10,000 kg x 2.42 = 24,200 kg CO2
Plant total: 25,620 / 20,000 = 1.281 kg CO2 per piece
Add clay transport and packing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
